content: The SEC63 translocation protein, also known as SEC63 homolog, is a protein in humans encoded by the SEC63 gene. The Sec61 complex serves as the central component of the protein translocation machinery within the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The protein encoded by the SEC63 gene, along with the SEC62 protein, has been identified as being associated with the ribosome-free Sec61 complex. It is hypothesized that the Sec61-Sec62-Sec63 complex facilitates post-translational protein translocation into the ER. Additionally, this complex may also be involved in the retrograde transport of ER proteins that are destined for degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent pathway. The protein encoded by the SEC63 gene is an integral membrane protein localized in the rough ER. Mutations in the SEC63 gene have been associated with autosomal dominant polycystic liver disease.
